label: def:forward_invariance
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:forward_invariance}
    A set \({\mathcal C} \subset \mathbb R^n\) is forward invariant with respect to \eqref{eq:dynamics} if \(x_0 \in {\mathcal C}\) implies \(x_k \in {\mathcal C}\) for all \(k \geq 0\).

label: lem:lambda_min_concave
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:lambda_min_concave}
    If \(H_i\) is matrix concave, then \(h_i(x) \triangleq \lambda_1(H_i(x))\) is concave and \({\mathcal S}_i = \{ x : h_i(x) \geq 0 \}\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since \(h_i(x) = \min_{\left \lVertv\right \rVert_2 = 1} v^\intercal H_i(x) v\) is a pointwise minimum of concave functions of \(x\), it is concave \cite[Sec. 3.2.3]{boyd2004convex}.
     
    The set identity holds since \(H_i(x) \succeq 0\) if and only if \(\lambda_1(H_i(x)) \geq 0\).
head: environment

label: prop:union
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By the Courant--Fischer theorem \cite[Thm. 4.2.6]{horn2012matrix}, \(\lambda_j(A) = \max_{Y \in \mathcal{O}_{p,r}} \lambda_1(Y^\intercal A Y)\) for \(A \in \mathbb{S}^p\), which gives \eqref{eq:S_j_union}.
     
    Each \(x \mapsto Y^\intercal H(x) Y\) is matrix concave by Section \ref{sec:prelim}, so its superlevel set is convex.
head: environment

label: lem:Phi_safe_subset
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Phi_safe_subset}
    \(\Phi_H\) is a safe subset function for \({\mathcal S}^{(j)}\) on \(\mathcal{D} = \mathbb R^n\).
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(x \in \mathbb R^n\) and \(z\) satisfy \(\Phi_H(z, x) \succeq 0\), that is, \(\lambda_1(Y(x)^\intercal H(z) Y(x)) \geq 0\).
     
    By Lemma \ref{lem:interlacing} with \(i = 1\), \(\lambda_1(Y(x)^\intercal H(z) Y(x)) \leq \lambda_{1+p-r}(H(z)) = \lambda_j(H(z))\), so \(z \in {\mathcal S}^{(j)}\), which verifies \eqref{eq:subset_property}.
     
    Finally, \(\Phi_H(x, x) = \Lambda(x) \succeq 0\) for all \(x \in {\mathcal S}^{(j)}\) by \eqref{eq:Lambda}.
head: environment

label: thm:main
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) The map \(u \mapsto Y(x_k)^\intercal H(f(x_k) + g(x_k) u) Y(x_k)\) is matrix concave by Section \ref{sec:prelim}, and the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:main_constraint} is constant in \(u\).
     
    (ii) By Lemma \ref{lem:Phi_safe_subset} and the standing feasibility assumption, \(\Phi_H\) is an SDTE-MCBF for \({\mathcal S}^{(j)}\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), and the claim follows from Theorem \ref{thm:SDTE_invariance}.
     
    (iii) Write \eqref{eq:main_constraint} at step \(k\) as \(Y_k^\intercal H(x_{k+1}) Y_k = (1-\gamma)\Lambda_k + B_k\) with \(B_k \succeq 0\).
     
    By Lemma \ref{lem:weyl}, \(\lambda_i(Y_k^\intercal H(x_{k+1}) Y_k) \geq (1-\gamma) \lambda_i(\Lambda_k) = (1-\gamma) \lambda_{i+j-1}(H(x_k))\) for \(i \in \{1,\ldots,r\}\).
     
    By Lemma \ref{lem:interlacing}, \(\lambda_i(Y_k^\intercal H(x_{k+1}) Y_k) \leq \lambda_{i+p-r}(H(x_{k+1})) = \lambda_{i+j-1}(H(x_{k+1}))\).
     
    Combining and reindexing gives \(\lambda_i(H(x_{k+1})) \geq (1-\gamma)\lambda_i(H(x_k))\) for \(i \in \{j,\ldots,p\}\), and \eqref{eq:eig_bound} follows by induction.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Theorem \ref{thm:main}(iii) does not require \(x_0 \in {\mathcal S}^{(j)}\).
     
    If \(\lambda_j(H(x_0)) < 0\), then \eqref{eq:eig_bound} shows that \(\lambda_j(H(x_k))\) converges exponentially to zero from below, so that \(x_k\) approaches \({\mathcal S}^{(j)}\) in the sense of the \(j\)th eigenvalue.
head: environment
name: Zeroing

title: Remark
body_md:
The selected subspace \(Y(x_k)\) changes with \(x_k\), and in the diagonal case \(r = 1\) the selected index \(i^* = \arg\max_i h_i(x_k)\) may switch between consecutive steps.
     
    Forward invariance is established pointwise at each step and is unaffected by switching.
     
    Switching affects only the conservatism of \eqref{eq:main_constraint}, since the trajectory is confined to the currently selected convex subset until the selection changes.
head: environment
name: Switching

title: Remark
body_md:
In \cite{usevitch2026dtmcbf}, safe subset functions are constructed by projection onto convex components of the unsafe set, and the question of whether other constructions exist is left open.
     
    The function \(\Phi_H\) in \eqref{eq:Phi_H} is a safe subset function obtained without projection, and Theorem \ref{thm:main} shows that the SDTE-MCBF framework applies to it directly.

name: Relation

label: prop:weyl_condition
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Write \eqref{eq:weyl_constraint} as \(H(x_{k+1}) = H(x_k) - \gamma \lambda_j(H(x_k)) I_p + B_k\) with \(B_k \succeq 0\).
     
    By Lemma \ref{lem:weyl}, \(\lambda_j(H(x_{k+1})) \geq \lambda_j(H(x_k)) - \gamma \lambda_j(H(x_k)) = (1-\gamma)\lambda_j(H(x_k))\), and the first claim follows by induction.
     
    For the second claim, compress \eqref{eq:weyl_constraint} by \(Y_k = Y(x_k)\) to obtain \(Y_k^\intercal H(x_{k+1}) Y_k \succeq \Lambda_k - \gamma \lambda_j(H(x_k)) I_r\).
     
    Since \(\Lambda_k \succeq \lambda_j(H(x_k)) I_r\), it holds that \(\Lambda_k - \gamma \lambda_j(H(x_k)) I_r \succeq \Lambda_k - \gamma \Lambda_k = (1-\gamma)\Lambda_k\), which is \eqref{eq:main_constraint}.
head: environment
